title: What's Your Money Personality? A 10-Question Quiz
description: Take the 10-question money personality quiz. Find out if you are a Saver, Spender, Avoider or Juggler, and which three guides to read first.
keywords: money personality quiz money personality types saver spender quiz financial personality test
takeaways: Ten quick questions sort your habits into four types: Saver, Spender, Avoider or Juggler.
Each type has a real strength and one thing to watch.
Your result comes with three guides to start with. Most people are a mix.
body:
Some people check their balance every day. Others would rather not look at all. Neither is a character flaw. They are habits, and once you can name yours, it gets much easier to pick the advice that actually fits you. This short quiz has ten questions and no wrong answers. Pick the answer that sounds most like you, not the one you think you should pick. It takes about two minutes. ## Take the quiz
1. Payday arrives. What is the first thing you usually do?
2. Your banking app shows your balance. How do you react?
3. Friends suggest a pricey night out you had not planned for. You...
4. A bill arrives higher than expected. Your first move is...
5. You receive an unexpected $100. It most likely goes on...
6. How would you describe your budgeting style?
7. Checking your card statement feels like...
8. A sale email offers 40% off, today only. You...
9. At the end of a typical month, your money...
10. Your biggest money stress is...

No JavaScript? Count which type you picked most, using the table under "Scoring by hand" at the end of this page. ## The four money personalities ### The Avoider You are not careless with money. You are often just tired of thinking about it, so bills, balances and statements get pushed to later, and later gets stressful. The relief you feel when you finally look is real, and it is available much more often than you think. **Your strength:** when you do sit down with your numbers, you are honest and quick to act. **Watch out for:** late fees and surprise balances grow in the dark, so small regular peeks beat one big reckoning. **Start with:** [the 20-minute monthly money review](/blog/monthly-money-review/), [the best free budgeting apps](/blog/best-free-budgeting-apps/) and [how to build an emergency fund on a small income](/blog/emergency-fund-on-a-small-income/). ### The Spender You enjoy your money, and there is nothing shameful in that. Your spending usually buys real pleasure, time with people and good memories. The trouble starts when the fun is unplanned and the essentials have to compete with it at the end of the month. **Your strength:** you are generous and quick to say yes to experiences, which is a good life to be living. **Watch out for:** in-the-moment buys stack up quietly, so give fun its own planned pot instead of letting it raid the bills money. **Start with:** [how to stop impulse spending](/blog/how-to-stop-impulse-spending/), [why your budget keeps failing](/blog/why-your-budget-keeps-failing/) and [the 50/30/20 rule](/blog/50-30-20-rule-explained/). ### The Saver You get a genuine buzz from watching a balance grow, and you are usually the friend with a backup plan. Your habits are solid. Your next step is usually about making saved money work a little harder, not squeezing your life any tighter. **Your strength:** consistency. Regular small transfers add up to real security over time. **Watch out for:** being so careful that you never spend on things you value, or leaving savings in a low-interest account out of habit. **Start with:** [what a high-yield savings account is](/blog/high-yield-savings-account/), [how to start investing with little money](/blog/start-investing-with-little-money/) and [sinking funds for beginners](/blog/sinking-funds-for-beginners/). ### The Juggler Your money life has a lot of moving parts: uneven income, several bills, maybe shared costs or more than one debt. You keep it all in the air through effort and memory, which works until one busy week drops a ball. You do not need more discipline. You need a system that holds some of this for you. **Your strength:** resourcefulness. You are good at solving money problems on the fly. **Watch out for:** relying on memory for due dates and balances. Write the whole picture down once and review it monthly. **Start with:** [how to budget with irregular income](/blog/budget-with-irregular-income/), the free [bill tracker](/blog/bill-tracker-template/) and [how to split bills with roommates](/blog/how-to-split-bills-with-roommates/). ## What to do with your result Your type is a starting point, not a label. Most people are a mix, and your answers can change as your life does. Pick one of the three reads for your type, do one small thing from it this week, and take the quiz again in a few months to see what has shifted. If you want a structured way to start, the [30-day money reset challenge](/blog/30-day-money-reset-challenge/) gives you one small task a day. ## Scoring by hand Find each question's row, look under the letter you picked (A is the first answer, D the last) and add a point to that type. | Question | A | B | C | D | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Saver | Spender | Avoider | Juggler | | 2 | Saver | Avoider | Spender | Juggler | | 3 | Juggler | Spender | Saver | Avoider | | 4 | Saver | Avoider | Spender | Juggler | | 5 | Saver | Spender | Saver | Juggler | | 6 | Juggler | Avoider | Spender | Saver | | 7 | Saver | Avoider | Spender | Juggler | | 8 | Juggler | Avoider | Spender | Saver | | 9 | Saver | Avoider | Spender | Juggler | | 10 | Saver | Avoider | Spender | Juggler | The type with the most points is yours. If two tie, read both. *This quiz is a fun starting point for thinking about your habits, not a psychological test or financial advice.*
